cyclones.name: In-Fa
cyclones.title: Typhoon In-Fa
cyclones.where: Typhoon In-Fa is about 4,000 km east of Siargao, almost stationary. It is getting closer to the Philippines.
cyclones.windline: Maximum winds about 157 km/h near the centre, gusts to 222 km/h.
cyclones.reachline: Strong winds (about 55 km/h or more) reach up to about 330 km from the centre. Storm-force winds (about 90 km/h or more) reach up to about 80 km.
cyclones.fcline: In 24 hours it is forecast to be about 3,850 km east of Siargao as a Typhoon (176 km/h).
cyclones.cross: Reported by RSMC Tokyo and GDACS. GDACS gives 250 km/h, measured over 1 minute, which normally reads higher than the 10-minute figure used here.

sources: Sources: no official airport report could be read at this check. The 36 airports have no official airport report, so they use the MET Norway location forecast (updated 9:17 PM to 9:18 PM) and are marked Estimate. Estimates show rain and wind only and cannot confirm thunderstorms, so an Estimate airport is never shown as Danger. For Estimates, bad weather means moderate or heavy rain (2.5 mm or more in an hour), or winds of 39 km/h or more. Tomorrow and days-ahead outlooks use the same airport forecasts and MET Norway estimates and are less certain than today's alerts. Typhoon watch compares three sources, checked 12:35 AM: aviation storm warnings (position, movement, warning areas), RSMC Tokyo of the Japan Meteorological Agency (strength, how far strong winds reach, 24-hour forecast) and GDACS (cross-check). Reached at this check: aviation storm warnings, RSMC Tokyo, GDACS. A cyclone is shown and alerted only when at least two of them report it. Earthquakes are from PHIVOLCS (magnitude 4.5 and stronger), data as of Oct 27, 12:35 AM. Accuracy ranking, highest first: 1) official airport report, 2) official airport forecast, 3) official aviation area warning, 4) computer forecast estimate. The moving rain layer on the map is a MET Norway forecast, rebuilt every few hours; it is a picture of the forecast and plays no part in the alert levels. When sources differ the higher-ranked one is used, and each airport's details show its confidence. If a source cannot be reached, its backup is used automatically and the Data sources table shows which one supplied the data. Times are Philippine time. Volcanoes: ash clouds and eruptions are from official aviation ash warnings (SIGMET) on aviationweather.gov, checked 12:35 AM. Volcano alert levels are from PHIVOLCS volcano bulletins.
